profile_slow_tests.test: Profile test suite to identify slowest tests (target: full suite < 5 min)
profile_slow_tests.approach: Run pytest --durations=20 to find slowest tests, then optimize or mark for CI-only
profile_slow_tests.note: Session 212: Profiled full suite. Top 4 slowest tests account for 624s (59%): test_what_happened_p95_under_500ms (341s), test_what_happened_with_1000_items (122s), test_all_query_methods_p95_combined (97s), test_combined_workload_with_large_dataset (62s). All are in test_integration_load.py. Additional slow tests: extraction_failures (18s each x5), security tests (10s). Recommendation: Mark load tests as @pytest.mark.slow for CI-only runs. Without load tests, suite would run ~7 minutes. With further optimization of extraction_failures mocking, target of <5 min is achievable.

profile_results.optimization_path: Mark test_integration_load.py as @pytest.mark.slow, optimize extraction_failures mocking, skip SentenceTransformer tests on CI (50 errors from meta tensor issue)

implementation: 1. Add meeting_date_ts (Unix timestamp) to _decision_to_metadata() in embeddings.py
2. Update search_decisions() to build where clause using {meeting_date_ts: {$gte: timestamp}}
3. Regenerate vector index with new metadata
4. Update history.py _search_semantic_decisions() to convert ISO date to timestamp for filtering
numeric_date_metadata.note: Session 195: Implemented. ChromaDB requires $and for combining $gte/$lte. Tests: test_search_with_date_range_filter_in_range, test_search_with_date_range_filter_out_of_range, test_search_with_since_only
